name: Ash Agyemang-Volkov-Echeverría
role: Personnel recovery and hostile extraction — extraction specialist
location: Kessler Row — arms dealers and augmentation clinics, near Halsted and Division
description:
Tui Bautista-Nwosu is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 43, the augmentation scarring around his temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ice in the brain — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in GLMZ, third generation — he has the city in his blood, its rhythms in his bones, its cruelty in his expectations. He works as a extraction specialist out of Kessler Row, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Tui Bautista-Nwosu has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and he cultivates ambiguity on the topic.

core_fears: Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
core_desires: Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of GLMZ
coping_mechanisms: Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
psychology.secret: Tui Bautista-Nwosu is slowly going chrome-sick — rejection symptoms are manageable now but getting worse. Has maybe two years before it becomes visible.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' — either royal or dissociative, nobody asks
example_lines: "We go in, we get the asset, we leave. Everything else is improvisation."
"The extraction window is four minutes. I've done it in three."
"I don't rescue people. I relocate them aggressively."

story_hooks: Tui Bautista-Nwosu discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
Tui Bautista-Nwosu's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
Someone is impersonating Tui Bautista-Nwosu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
narrative_function: Tui Bautista-Nwosu is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
augmentations: Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain. Cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic, obvious chrome
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.

strengths: mechanical aptitude — can repair or modify almost anything
weaknesses: risk-averse to the point of missed opportunities

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
habits: Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Practices a kata or fighting form every morning regardless of circumstances
breaking_points: Their body rejecting their cyberware — chrome rot, immune rejection, the nightmare scenario
Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong
Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out

physical_description.heritage: Mixed ancestry reflecting Sub-Saharan African (32.9%), Hispanic/Latin American (28.0%), East Asian (17.8%), Eastern European (17.3%), and Northern European (4.0%) heritage. The genetic blend produces a uniquely cosmopolitan phenotype—African-derived bone structure and warm skin undertones combined with East Asian eye shape characteristics and subtle Eastern European features in the cheekbones and jaw structure.
physical_description.build: Rawboned and lean—the muscular definition of someone who carries minimal excess mass. Broad shoulders narrowing to a tight waist. The physiology reads as economically built for endurance and speed rather than raw strength, though the visible chrome arm compensates for any deficit.
physical_description.hair_style: Short, practical cut—maintained but not groomed. Starts to gray at the temples.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint amber circuitry visible at the outer iris edges—subcutaneous neural interface bleed-through
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-warm brown with subtle golden undertones, sun-weathered from decades in the GLMZ. The tone reflects the harmonious blend of Sub-Saharan and Latin American ancestry with hint of East Asian warmth.
physical_description.complexion: Angular face with pronounced cheekbones and strong jawline characteristic of mixed African and Hispanic heritage, refined by Eastern European bone structure. Weathered skin shows fine lines around the eyes and mouth—the kind accumulated from squinting in bad light and years of low-grade stress. Minimal facial hair, kept trimmed close. The scarring around his temples and jawline is deliberate and visible: installation scars from neural work, pale threads of scar tissue running from his right temple toward his ear and along the underside of his jaw where augmentation hardware meets bone.
distinguishing_marks: Pale surgical scarring along the right temple, approximately 8cm in length, extending toward the ear—neural dampener installation site
Matching scarline along the right jawline beneath the ear, roughly 6cm—neural interface anchor point
Small burn scar on the left forearm, roughly 3cm diameter, circular—old accident or deliberate
Thin white line across the inside of the right wrist where the cybernetic arm interfaces with residual organic tissue
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Full chromatic replacement of the right arm from shoulder joint downward—brushed steel and gunmetal gray with articulated finger joints and reinforced knuckle plating. The shoulder joint is clearly mechanical, visible beneath the skin at the clavicle junction. Neural dampener hardware visible at both temples as faint metallic threading beneath the skin and scar tissue. Circuitry bleed-through at the eyes suggests deeper neural integration.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight slightly forward, shoulders relaxed but ready. Moves economically—no wasted motion. The right arm has a subtle mechanical lag in certain movements, a fraction of a second delay in fine motor control that he's learned to compensate for. When thinking, he favors tilting his head to the left, unconsciously favoring his organic side. Baseline posture suggests someone perpetually half-ready for immediate action.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian—function-first without pretense. Black reinforced cargo pants with extra pockets and subdued gray stitching. Steel-toed boots, scuffed and re-heeled multiple times. Usually wears a lightweight tactical jacket in dark gray or black, synthetic materials rated for minor impact resistance, with internal pockets for tools and hardware. Under that, simple t-shirts in neutral colors, sometimes with faint logos from defunct GLMZ establishments. No jewelry except a chipped plasteel watch on his left wrist. Clothing bears the wear of actual use—small tears carefully patched, stains that won't come out, the overall appearance of someone who can't afford to replace things and doesn't care how it looks as long as it functions.
